---
title: "Validation"
---

Compare adjusted flows with a benchmark on matching OD keys. Source and time
columns contribute to the identity of repeated observations. Missing benchmark
pairs and omitted zero flows change the evaluation population; inspect matched
rows and choose filtering explicitly.

```python
from debiaspy import (
    adjust_inverse_penetration, debiaspy_example_data, validate_flow_overall,
)

bundle = debiaspy_example_data(n_areas=25)
adjusted = adjust_inverse_penetration(bundle["mpd_od"], bundle["coverage"])
result = validate_flow_overall(
    adjusted, bundle["benchmark_od"],
    comparisons=["raw_vs_benchmark", "adjusted_vs_benchmark"],
    drop_zeros=False, na_rm=False,
)
print(result["summary"])
```

`validate_flow_pairs` provides paired rows, `validate_flow_margins` checks
origin/destination totals, `validate_flow_distribution` compares shares, and
`validate_flow_residuals` summarises errors. `validate_flow_residual_structure`
adds spatial diagnostics when you supply area-neighbour links. Its permutation
seed reproduces Python results; R and NumPy use different random streams.

The corresponding `*_methods` helpers compare mappings of method names to
adjusted DataFrames. They identify the failing method when an input is invalid.
Use `validate_flow_prepare_outputs` if adjusted results need their raw flows
attached. Preserve undefined adjusted rows in exported results and explain
any filtering before reporting accuracy.
